findings.title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting on every translation
findings.body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym to build the chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] for every missing-key lookup, so this puts a SiteSetting (DB/Redis/cache) read on the hot translation path and will also fail during boot/asset-precompile when the DB is unavailable. Cache the site default per-request or memoize it instead of reading it per lookup.

findings.title: Translate only preloads current locale, not fallbacks
findings.body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate calls load_locale(config.locale) only for the active locale. Fallback locales (site default and :en) are only preloaded in ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Any translation outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, console, rake) will therefore resolve fallbacks against unloaded translation files and return missing-translation errors even though the fallback string exists.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain
findings.body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb the cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" with no component for the fallback chain. A key that fell back to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en is cached under just key+locale, so changing SiteSetting.default_locale (or loading a previously-missing fallback file) leaves stale fallback values in the 300-entry ThreadSafeCache until process restart or I18n.reload!. Include the resolved fallback locales or default-locale version in the cache key or invalidate the cache on locale-setting change.
